EDUCATIONAL PHILOSOPHY

BUILT FOR THE NEXT GENERATION OF FITNESS PROFESSIONALS.

True fitness coaching requires more than memorizing workout templates. At Kynetiq, we bridge the gap between human biomechanics, physical therapy-informed movement screening, and practical coaching on the gym floor.

Whether you want to work in top athletic clubs, lead specialized personal training, or build an independent fitness coaching practice, our educational framework emphasizes structured foundational science, supervised hands-on practice, and clear client communication.

FLAGSHIP CERTIFICATION

3-MONTH CERTIFIED GYM TRAINER COURSE

An intensive 12-week curriculum designed to take aspiring fitness enthusiasts from core movement anatomy to confident floor coaching.

PRACTICAL, SCIENCE-BACKED TRAINER PREPARATION

Developed specifically for the evolving Indian fitness industry, this course focuses on what happens when real clients walk into a gym: assessing movement limitations, teaching compound lifts safely, and designing progressive routines that deliver results without injury.

PROPOSED LEARNING MODULES Subject to Academy Confirmation

The curriculum below represents our recommended standard structure for comprehensive trainer education:

Skeletal and muscular anatomy, joint actions, planes of motion, and force vectors during human movement.

  • Bone landmarks & joint classification
  • Agonist, antagonist & stabilizer mechanics
  • Spine mechanics & intra-abdominal pressure
  • Levers and torque in barbell lifting

Mastery of fundamental movement patterns: Squat, Hinge, Push, Pull, Lunge, and Carry under expert supervision.

  • Barbell squat setups & common compensations
  • Conventional vs. Romanian deadlift execution
  • Overhead press mobility requirements
  • Verbal and tactile coaching cues

Understanding movement screening, common gym injuries (shoulder impingement, lower back discomfort), and active recovery principles.

  • Postural screening & joint mobility testing
  • Scapular stability & rotator cuff mechanics
  • Modifying exercises for client comfort
  • When to refer out to licensed physiotherapists

Building periodized 8-week routines, tracking progressive overload, conducting client consultations, and gym floor etiquette.

  • Periodization for hypertrophy & strength
  • Consultation techniques & goal setting
  • Client retention & professional standards
  • Practical floor evaluation preparation
